newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan money growth less than expected--analysts.
newsitem.headline: Japan money growth less than expected--analysts.

text.p: Japan's money supply growth in September was less than expected and the outlook for the indicator has turned gloomy as bank lending to private corporations remained sluggish, economists said on Thursday.

"From money supply results alone, it's difficult to judge that the overall economy is starting to slow down again. But I'm worried about the lower-than-expected results," said Hiroshi Miyazaki, an economist at Yamaichi Research Institute.
Japan's broadly defined money supply average of M2 plus certificates of deposit (M2+CDs) grew a preliminary 3.5 percent in September from a year earlier, the Bank of Japan said.
Economists polled by Reuters had predicted growth of around 3.6 to 3.7 percent for September. In August, money supply grew 3.7 percent from a year earlier.
"The fall in money supply growth is somewhat worrisome for the outlook of the economy," said Yoshito Sakakibara, market analyst at Salomon Brothers Asia Ltd.
However, he said mid-year fiscal book closings in September might have helped push down money supply growth for the month.
"The outlook for money supply doesn't look too strong, but we need to look at further months," he said.
A BOJ official told reporters after the data was released that there was no change in the trend of money supply growth, even though September M2+CDs had fallen 0.2 percentage point from August.

The official said bank loans to the private sector remained sluggish and a shift of funds from money management funds to commercial bank deposits -- a factor that pushed up the growth in July and August -- slowed in September.
However, he said M2+CDs grew a preliminary 3.6 percent during the July-September period, in line with the central bank's earlier forecast. He said he did not see any change in the trend.
